cell_type: trophosome cells, vestimentum cells, plume cells

Riftia specimens were dissected onboard, and samples from four different organs (here referred to as tissues) were stored at –80°C: the lamellae of the tentacular crown were shaved off to provide plume samples, trophosome samples were dissected from whole trophosome, body wall samples were retrieved and washed after removal of the trophosome, and vestimental samples were cut off from the lateral portions of the vestimentum.
material_type: Sampling dates for all Riftia tissue samples for proteomics, transcriptomics, and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) are summarized in Table S1e in the supplemental material.
sample_source: Riftia samples were obtained during several research cruises in 2008, 2014, and 2017, with RV Atlantis, to the deep-sea hydrothermal vent fields on the East Pacific Rise at 9°50′N, 104°17′W.
species: To identify host-symbiont interaction mechanisms, we therefore sequenced the Riftia transcriptome, which served as a basis for comparative metaproteomic analyses of symbiont-containing versus symbiont-free tissues, both under energy-rich and energy-limited conditions.
tissue: For metaproteomics analysis, we used three biological replicates per tissue (trophosome, vestimentum, and plume) and condition (specimens with S-rich and S-depleted trophosomes), which resulted in a total of 18 samples.
